q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT DISTINCT(A.EMAIL) AS EMAIL FROM (SELECT EMAIL, COUNT(EMAIL) AS CNT FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL) AS A WHERE CNT > 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT(A.EMAIL) AS EMAIL FROM (SELECT EMAIL, COUNT(EMAIL) AS CNT FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL) AS A WHERE CNT > 1
explanation: Q1 groups by EMAIL and selects EMAIL where the count of EMAIL is greater than 1, which will return all duplicate emails. Q2 first groups by EMAIL and counts the occurrences, then selects distinct emails where the count is greater than 1. The difference arises because Q2 uses DISTINCT, which removes duplicates from the final result, while Q1 does not.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two duplicate emails, and the final result of Q1 should contain both duplicates, while Q2 should contain only one of the duplicates due to the DISTINCT keyword.
